name: Persistent Petitioners
oracle_text:
{1}, {T}: Target player mills a card. (They put the top card of their library into their graveyard.)
Tap four untapped Advisors you control: Target player mills twelve cards.
A deck can have any number of cards named Persistent Petitioners.
blocked_sentences: A deck can have any number of cards named Persistent Petitioners.

needs.what:
a residual-gate claimant for the printed deck-construction sentence, exactly the entry `verify._covered` already keeps for every other line no ability can carry (kicker, multikicker, gift, ascend, cost_reduction, emerge, evoke, bestow, additional_cost, uncounterable, devoid). One branch: `if card.any_number_in_deck and stripped.lower().startswith("a deck can have any number of cards named"): return True`, strict the way bestow's and devoid's claimants are -- `CardDef.any_number_in_deck` only returns True when the name inside the printed sentence is the card's OWN name, so the words cannot be claimed without the rule behind them, and Nazgul's "up to nine" still fails the gate rather than being laundered through. Everything else about this card is already expressible and verified: with that one branch patched in memory, the payload below passes all six gates unchanged. Ship the card with it.

needs.why_existing_wont_do: The sentence is rule 903.5b's deck-construction exception, and the engine already implements it: `CardDef.any_number_in_deck` (src/automtg/engine/carddef.py) parses the printed line and `registry.validate_deck` honours it, so a twenty-Petitioners deck imports as the legal deck it is. There is nothing left for the card to say -- and nothing it *can* say. `claimed_lines` consumes a line three ways and none reaches this one: `lift_keywords` needs a line that is nothing but ability keywords, `spell_effects` only blanket-claims lines on an instant or sorcery, and `_covered` needs either a card-level claimant (there is none for this field) or an ability whose `text` is the line. No ability can honestly be that ability: an AbilityModel is activated, triggered or static; `_compile_static` refuses a static without an `effect` from STATIC_EFFECTS and none of the 44 says anything about deck construction; and an activated or triggered ability carrying the line would be a card that mills or taps when the printed sentence does nothing during a game at all. Writing the line onto ability 2's `text` -- the only other way past `_covered`, which also matches a printed line contained in a longer claim -- is the laundering the gate exists to catch, and would leave a line nobody implements looking implemented. Verified empirically rather than reasoned: the payload above fails `verify` at gate 3 with "printed text not represented: A deck can have any number of cards named", and passes all six gates the moment the one `_covered` branch exists. Same shape as d4af1b3c (bestow -- "the printed cost the residual gate could not hear") and e4987745 (a spell that exiles itself), both of which were closed by adding the missing claimant rather than by bending the card.
